under-eye-filler-tear-trough.summary: Filler placed in the hollow under the eyes to soften shadows and dark circles, so you look more rested; the change shows right after treatment.

quick.overview:
Tear trough filler is a soft gel, usually hyaluronic acid, placed in the groove between the lower eyelid and the cheek. The payoff people want is a smoother under-eye area with less hollowing and less of the shadow that makes eyes look tired, without lower eyelid surgery.

The filler adds volume under the skin, which camouflages the hollow and the bulge of orbital fat that casts the shadow [1]. Clinicians use it widely as a non-surgical option. A systematic review of 42 articles on hyaluronic acid tear trough techniques found no standardized approach, and a case series of 198 eyes in 100 patients evaluated it as an alternative to lower eyelid surgery. On looksmaxxing forums it is described as a small change that shows in person without looking overdone.
quick.how: It is done in a clinic by a trained injector, usually as a short appointment with the result visible straight away once initial swelling settles. People often pair it with cheek filler or skincare for the under-eye area. Results from hyaluronic acid filler are temporary and are topped up over time.
quick.risks: Swelling after treatment is common; in one retrospective review of 706 treatments it occurred in over half of patients. Delayed lumps, discoloration and xanthelasma-like reactions are described in a systematic review of delayed complications. Rare orbital events have been reported, including a case of orbital compartment syndrome with bleeding behind the eye that resolved without lasting visual loss [5]. The area is technically demanding, so injector skill matters.

angle.text: Filler fills the tear trough hollow so the shadowing under your eyes softens and the area looks smoother and more rested. The change is visible right after treatment. Reviews describe it as common but technically demanding.

liposuction-chin-lipo.summary: Surgical suction removal of fat under the chin and neck to sharpen the jawline and neck angle; removed fat cells do not return.

quick.overview:
Liposuction removes localized fat through a thin suction tube (cannula) inserted via small incisions. Under the chin and along the neck, the payoff people want is less submental fullness and a sharper jawline and neck angle, sometimes combined with chin surgery.

The cannula is moved through the fat layer to remove cells, often after fluid with dilute anaesthetic is injected (the tumescent technique) [11]. Removed fat cells do not regrow, though remaining fat cells can enlarge, and reference sources say overall body fat generally returns to its earlier level over months. The neck contour shows once swelling settles. A 2004 randomized study found liposuction did not alter insulin action or coronary risk factors. Evidence specific to submental liposuction comes from small registered studies and clinical practice.
quick.how: It is performed by a surgeon, often with local anaesthesia and sedation for small areas like the chin, and sometimes alongside a chin implant or neck lift. People wear a compression garment for a period afterward, and swelling takes weeks to settle before the final contour shows.
quick.risks: A 2024 meta-analysis of 39 studies and 29,368 patients found contour deformity (2.35 percent), hyperpigmentation (1.49 percent), seroma (0.65 percent) and haematoma (0.27 percent) among complications [1]. Rarer serious events include deep vein thrombosis, organ perforation and embolism, with risk rising with the volume removed [11]. It is surgery under anaesthesia and should be done by a licensed surgeon.

angle.text: Fat is suctioned from under the chin and neck, reducing submental fullness so the jawline and neck angle look sharper. Removed fat cells do not return, and the contour shows once swelling settles.

otoplasty-ear-pinning.summary: Surgery that sets protruding ears closer to the head for a more balanced face from the front; long established, with high reported satisfaction.

quick.overview:
Otoplasty reshapes or repositions the cartilage of the outer ear. For prominent ears it restores the fold of the antihelix, reduces a deep conchal bowl or repositions a protruding lobe, bringing the ear closer to the head. The payoff people want is a less prominent ear profile and a more balanced face from the front.

Prominent ears are the most common abnormality of the external ear, and more than 200 techniques have been described. Reviews describe generally high patient satisfaction, though a 2005 review concluded no technique is definitive, and the evidence is mostly case series and expert reviews. On looksmaxxing forums it is often described as a relatively low-cost add-on, frequently mentioned alongside jaw surgery and rhinoplasty.
quick.how: Surgeons either use stitches that bend the cartilage into a fold, score or cut the cartilage so it bends back, or remove part of the conchal cartilage. Some centres offer closed or minimally invasive versions. A head band is typically worn for several weeks afterward to protect the shape, and the result is visible once healed.
quick.risks: Documented complications include hematoma, infection, suture extrusion, scarring, recurrence of prominence and overcorrection with an unnatural, pinned-looking contour. A large case review of 562 patients reported significant morbidity including residual deformity. Revision surgery for lobe or helix irregularities is discussed. It is surgery performed by licensed surgeons.

angle.text: Ears are set closer to the head, giving a less prominent ear profile and a more balanced face from the front. Forum posters describe it as an add-on to jaw surgery, and the change is visible once healed.

gold-thread-lift.summary: Fine gold threads implanted under the skin in the hope of smoother, tighter skin and fewer wrinkles; studied in a small clinical series.

quick.overview:
Gold thread implantation places very fine strands of gold under the skin, historically in parts of Asia, aiming for tighter skin, fewer wrinkles or a lifting effect on the face. Looksmaxxing discussion of it is sparse.

Proponents describe the threads as stimulating the skin or supporting tissue, and a histopathology study examined skin that had gold threads implanted for facial rejuvenation. One series of 78 patients in Archives of Plastic Surgery looked at gold thread implantation for crow's feet. Most other literature is case reports of threads found on X-rays or CT scans years after treatment.
quick.how: Threads are inserted under the skin by a practitioner, in cosmetic clinics or acupuncture-style settings. It is sometimes mentioned as an alternative to thread lifts. Gold threads are permanent, so they stay in place after the visible effect has been and gone.
quick.risks: Case reports describe threads migrating, recurrent cellulitis, and incidental findings on imaging that can be mistaken for other conditions or obscure dental imaging. In one fatal case report, gold threads were found at autopsy alongside electroacupuncture injuries; the report attributed the death to pneumothoraces from electroacupuncture, not the threads. Because the threads are permanent, they cannot simply be left to dissolve.

angle.text: Gold threads placed under the skin are promoted for smoother, tighter skin and fewer wrinkles through a skin reaction around the threads. A small series of 78 patients studied it for crow's feet, and case reports describe threads staying in place for years.

pdo-thread-lift.summary: Absorbable polydioxanone threads placed under the skin to lift sagging cheeks, jawline and neck, with immediate improvement reported.

quick.overview:
A PDO thread lift uses dissolvable polydioxanone sutures, sometimes with barbs or cones, placed under the skin to reposition sagging tissue in the midface, jowls or neck without a facelift incision. The payoff people want is a sharper jawline and lifted cheeks with little downtime.

The threads are anchored to tissue and mechanically suspend it, and absorbable materials dissolve over time. A 2025 systematic review of twelve studies covering 818 patients reported improved aesthetic scores such as GAIS and FACE-Q in all cases immediately after the procedure, while noting that earlier studies had not shown long-term efficacy for absorbable threads. A study of PLLA/PLGA-containing threads found collagen stimulation in biopsies.
quick.how: It is done in a clinic as a short procedure with local numbing, with threads placed through fine entry points. People use it as a temporary lift or jawline enhancer and as a lower-downtime alternative to a surgical facelift. Results are described as short-lived compared with surgery.
quick.risks: Reviews describe mostly minor, self-limiting events such as bruising, swelling and asymmetry. A BBC investigation reported in Wikipedia found UK training courses with no mandatory qualifications and poor infection control in an undercover recording, and one physician quoted called it the most dangerous aesthetic procedure because threads cannot be removed. PDO threads are medical devices that should be placed by trained clinicians.

angle.text: Absorbable threads suspend sagging tissue, repositioning the cheeks, jawline and neck for a lifted look with little downtime. Improvement is reported immediately after treatment; reviews note long-term data are limited.

fox-eye-thread-lift.summary: Clinic threads that raise the outer brow and eye corner for an upturned fox eye tilt; the lift is visible after treatment.

quick.overview:
The fox eye look is an upward-slanting, elongated eye shape with a lifted outer corner and brow tail. The thread version uses absorbable threads, usually PDO, placed around the brow and temple to pull tissue up and outward in a clinic.

The term comes from social media and cosmetic clinic marketing, and on looksmaxxing forums where related options include tape and canthoplasty. Thread lifts in general suspend soft tissue by anchoring absorbable sutures under the skin; here the aim is raising the lateral brow and eye corner. A separate laser protocol called the fox eyes lift, using Er:YAG and Nd:YAG wavelengths, has been studied in a split-face study for eyebrow elevation. No published trial tests threads for this specific look.
quick.how: It is a short in-clinic procedure with threads placed around the brow and temple, and clinics report the lift is visible afterward. Some people compare it with taping at home or with surgical canthoplasty, which is a different and more invasive route to the same shape.
quick.risks: Reviews of thread lifts in general describe mostly minor, self-limiting events. The area around the eye has delicate tissue, and surgical fox eye procedures such as canthoplasty have drawn commentary, including a study that rated YouTube content on aesthetic canthoplasty as mostly poor quality and advertising-oriented. Threads are medical devices placed by clinicians.

angle.text: Absorbable threads lift the outer brow, tilting the eye corner upward for a foxy, upturned eye shape. Clinics report the lift is visible after treatment; no published study tests threads for this specific look.

brazilian-butt-lift.summary: Fat taken by liposuction and injected into the buttocks to add volume and reshape the waist-to-hip silhouette using your own fat.

quick.overview:
A Brazilian butt lift takes fat from elsewhere on the body by liposuction and injects it into the buttocks. The payoff people want is fuller, rounder glutes and a reshaped waist-to-hip silhouette, using their own tissue rather than an implant.

Fat is harvested, processed and injected into buttock tissue. Surgical reviews describe gluteal fat grafting as the fastest growing procedure in body contouring, with much of the recent literature on safety, anatomy and technique. Some transferred fat is reabsorbed, so volume can change over following months. On looksmaxxing forums it is discussed mainly as a female-appearance procedure, with some users asking about male equivalents.
quick.how: It is done by a plastic surgeon under anaesthesia, combining liposuction of donor areas with injection into the glutes. Swelling takes weeks to settle before the shape shows, and some people have repeat sessions. Some surgeons use ultrasound to visualise the injection plane. Travel for the procedure is covered in media reports.
quick.risks: Reported complications include fat resorption, asymmetry, infection, seroma and persistent numbness. A 2015 report from Mexican surgeons recorded 13 deaths from gluteal lipoinjection, and a 2019 meta-analysis reported complication rates of 7% for fat grafting versus 31% for implants. Safety technique has become a central focus of the field. It is a surgical procedure for licensed surgeons.

angle.text: Fat harvested by liposuction is injected into the glutes, adding volume and reshaping the waist-to-hip silhouette with your own tissue. The change shows once swelling settles; surgical reviews also document deaths, and safety technique is a major focus.

facelift-neck-lift.summary: Surgical lifting of the face and neck that tightens deeper tissue and removes excess skin for a younger, more defined jaw and neck.

quick.overview:
A facelift (rhytidectomy) repositions and tightens facial tissue and usually removes excess skin for a more youthful contour; a neck lift addresses the jawline and neck, often by treating the platysma muscle. They are often combined. The payoff is reduced jowls and neck laxity, and a more defined lower face.

Techniques range from skin-only lifts to SMAS and deep plane lifts that reposition deeper layers, with neck work such as platysma plication or submental liposuction. Recent literature emphasises restoring volume and lifting vertically. A review of facelift controversies concluded that available techniques are generally equal in efficacy. On looksmaxxing forums it is discussed by older men and people who have lost weight, often alongside jaw surgery or fat grafting.
quick.how: It is performed by a surgeon under anaesthesia, with incisions hidden around the ears and hairline. Recovery takes weeks, with the result visible after healing. Wikipedia cites typical skin-only results lasting 5 to 10 years, and people weigh surgery against fillers or threads.
quick.risks: Documented complications include hematoma (the most common), nerve injury, skin necrosis (higher in smokers), scarring, hair loss at incisions and changes in ear position. Wikipedia reports the ideal age for a facelift, by patient satisfaction, as 50 or younger. It is major surgery for licensed surgeons.

angle.text: Deeper tissues are tightened and skin redraped, reducing jowls and neck laxity for a younger, more defined jaw and neck. The change is visible after healing, and decades of published technique and complication data exist.

fractional-laser-resurfacing.summary: Clinic laser that treats skin in tiny columns to remodel acne scars, texture and sun damage, with improvement building over weeks.

quick.overview:
Fractional laser resurfacing treats a grid of microscopic columns of skin and leaves tissue between them intact. Dermatologists and plastic surgeons use it for acne scars, other scars, wrinkles, sun damage, stretch marks and uneven texture, with the payoff of smoother skin and fainter scars.

Ablative lasers (CO2 and erbium) vaporize microscopic channels, while non-ablative fractional lasers such as the 1550 nm devices heat the dermis without removing the surface. The controlled injury is described as stimulating new collagen and remodeling of the dermis, and because only a fraction of the surface is treated, healing is faster than with older fully ablative resurfacing. Clinical studies and randomized trials cover several scar types, with improvement typically gradual over multiple sessions.
quick.how: Treatments are done in clinics, often as a series of sessions. Ablative versions bring several days of visible wounding and recovery; non-ablative versions have less downtime. In looksmaxxing communities it sits in the clinic-based hardmaxx tier of skin treatment, and users describe heavy downtime.
quick.risks: Reported effects include redness, swelling, crusting, acne flares, herpes simplex reactivation, pigment changes and scarring. Dermatology reviews describe skin phototype (Fitzpatrick scale) as relevant to predicting outcomes, with pigment problems documented especially in darker skin. Devices are regulated medical devices operated by licensed clinicians.

angle.text: The laser creates microscopic treated zones, and collagen remodels as the skin heals, leaving smoother texture and fainter scars. Trials support it for several scar types, with improvement building over weeks after a period of downtime.

professional-microneedling-rf-microneedl.summary: Clinic treatment using fine needles, sometimes with radiofrequency, to trigger collagen and smooth acne scars, texture and fine lines.

quick.overview:
Professional microneedling uses a device with many fine needles to make controlled punctures in the skin; RF microneedling adds radiofrequency energy through the needles. Clinics offer it for acne scars, fine lines, skin laxity, enlarged pores and texture, with the payoff of smoother skin and softer scars.

The needles create small channels and a wound-healing response described as stimulating collagen and elastin production, and RF versions heat the dermis around the needle tips. Trials have tested it for acne scars, melasma, skin laxity and hair loss, and combined with platelet-rich plasma or exosomes. Systematic reviews report it as efficacious in melasma but not clearly better than topical hydroquinone, and a review found evidence for adding PRP to microneedling for acne scars less supportive than for PRP with fractional laser.
quick.how: Done in a dermatology or aesthetic clinic, usually as a series of sessions, with serums or PRP sometimes applied during treatment. On looksmaxxing forums it is often compared with at-home dermarolling, and some users recommend clinic RF treatment over deeper home needling. Redness settles over a few days.
quick.risks: Reported effects include redness, swelling and pinpoint bleeding, with infection and scarring possible. In 2024 the US CDC reported HIV infections linked to a spa offering PRP microneedling facials, prompting warnings about non-clinical settings. Devices and sterile technique matter, and licensed clinicians should perform it.

angle.text: Needles trigger the skin's healing response so new collagen forms, smoothing texture and softening scars over weeks. Trials support scar and texture use; claims about denser beard, eyebrow or scalp hair have been studied less.

medical-tourism-turkey-istanbul-korea.summary: Travelling abroad, often to Turkey or South Korea, for cosmetic surgery, hair transplants or dental work at lower prices, often bundled in one trip.

quick.overview:
Medical tourism means travelling to another country for non-emergency care. In appearance culture it usually means surgery, hair transplants and dental work in places such as Istanbul, Antalya or South Korea, where prices can be lower than at home and procedures can be combined into one trip.

In appearance-focused communities, Turkey is known for hair transplants and dental veneers and crowns, and South Korea for facial cosmetic surgery. The trip is a way of accessing procedures rather than an appearance change itself. Public-health reviews of medical tourism describe benefits such as access and cost alongside complications and continuity-of-care problems; evidence is mainly reviews, case series and scoping studies.
quick.how: People usually book through clinics or agents for a package that can include surgery, accommodation and transfers, and return home within days to weeks. Follow-up after return is arranged with local clinicians, if at all.
quick.risks: Reviews report infections (including outbreaks of fungal meningitis linked to cosmetic surgery in Mexico), difficulty arranging follow-up, and possible clotting risks from long flights after surgery. Legal recourse and insurance coverage for complications can be limited. Regulation differs by country; Turkey introduced a regulation on international health tourism in 2017.

angle.text: Looksmaxxers travel to Turkey or South Korea to access cosmetic surgery, hair transplants and dental work at lower prices, often combining procedures in one trip. The trip itself changes nothing; the procedures do. Reviews discuss infection and follow-up-care issues.

gastric-sleeve.summary: Bariatric surgery that removes most of the stomach for large, sustained weight loss, which also leans out the body and face.

quick.overview:
Sleeve gastrectomy removes most of the stomach, leaving a narrow tube. It is a medical treatment for severe obesity and, according to Wikipedia, the most commonly performed bariatric operation worldwide. The appearance payoff people link to it is large fat loss, giving a leaner body and slimmer face.

Removing roughly three quarters or more of the stomach limits how much food can be eaten and removes the part that produces the appetite hormone ghrelin. Research also describes effects on gut hormones and glucose handling beyond weight loss alone. Systematic reviews report weight loss and resolution of conditions like type 2 diabetes comparable to gastric bypass. It is studied as a medical treatment, not a cosmetic one, and no studies on appearance outcomes were identified.
quick.how: It is usually done laparoscopically under general anaesthesia, with eligibility set by clinical guidelines based on body mass index and health conditions. Afterwards people follow staged diets and vitamin supplementation, and weight loss builds over many months.
quick.risks: Documented risks include staple-line leaks, bleeding, clots, infection, reflux, nausea and vomiting, vitamin and thiamine deficiencies (including rare Wernicke encephalopathy), gastric dilation, and weight regain that may lead to revision surgery. The operation is considered irreversible.

angle.text: A reduced stomach leads to large, sustained weight loss, which users link to a leaner body and slimmer face. It is studied for weight loss and diabetes in severe obesity, with documented surgical and nutritional risks.

veneers-turkey-teeth.summary: Thin ceramic or composite shells bonded over teeth for a whiter, straighter-looking smile, visible straight away and durable in studies.

quick.overview:
Veneers are thin shells of porcelain or composite resin bonded to the front of teeth to change colour, shape or apparent alignment. The payoff people want is a uniform, brighter, straighter-looking smile. Multi-tooth makeovers are called Hollywood smile treatments, and Turkey teeth is a nickname for veneers or crowns from low-cost dental clinics in Turkey.

A 2025 systematic review and meta-analysis of 29 studies reported pooled survival of about 96% for feldspathic, 94% for leucite-reinforced and 97% for lithium disilicate veneers at around 10 years. A 2024 narrative review found similar survival, with dentin exposure lowering success. On looksmaxxing forums veneers are described as a high-impact change to facial appearance, sometimes as a stand-in for orthodontics.
quick.how: The dentist usually removes a thin layer of enamel (the amount varies, and some systems use little or none), takes an impression or digital scan, and bonds a veneer made in a lab or chairside. The change is visible straight away. Some people combine the work with a trip to Turkey, where multi-tooth packages are offered.
quick.risks: Reported complications include chipping, debonding, marginal staining, sensitivity and decay. Preparation that exposes dentin is associated with lower success rates, and enamel lost in preparation does not regrow. Critics cited by Wikipedia describe overuse on healthy teeth as instant orthodontics.

angle.text: Shells bonded over your teeth unify colour, shape and alignment for a whiter, straighter-looking smile, visible straight away. Reviews report high survival over about a decade, and preparation can remove enamel.

calf-implants.summary: Silicone implants placed in the lower leg to add calf volume, used for thin calves, asymmetry and bodybuilding size.

quick.overview:
Calf implants are silicone prostheses placed under the fascia or muscle of the lower leg to add volume. People use them for thin calves that do not respond to training, for asymmetry or wasting, and bodybuilders seek them for size. The payoff is larger, more muscular-looking calves.

Implants were first reported in 1979. Surgeons have published single-center series and a 2019 review pooling 26 studies on 1,498 patients and 2,629 calves. Fat grafting and combined approaches are also described as alternatives. The evidence is surgeon-reported case series and reviews rather than controlled trials, and looksmaxxing forum discussion is limited.
quick.how: A surgeon makes an incision, typically behind the knee, and places a solid or gel-filled silicone implant beneath the fascia or in a plane between the calf muscles. The added volume shows after healing, with a period of restricted activity beforehand.
quick.risks: The 26-study review analysed complication rates by technique. Reported problems include seroma, implant displacement, capsular contracture, dissatisfaction leading to removal and, in one case, acute compartment syndrome with muscle necrosis. Regulation of implants and surgeons varies by country.

angle.text: A silicone implant placed in the calf adds lower-leg volume for larger, more muscular-looking calves, visible after healing. Evidence comes from surgical case series and a 26-study review.

pec-bicep-implants.summary: Solid silicone implants placed over muscle to add chest or arm bulk and definition surgically.

quick.overview:
Pectoral and bicep implants are solid silicone pieces placed under or around muscle to make it look bigger and more defined. Pectoral implants were first used for chest wall reconstruction and later for cosmetic chest contouring. The payoff people want is a fuller upper body where training has not produced the size.

The implant sits in a surgically created pocket, typically beneath the pectoralis major, and adds volume and shape from underneath. Pectoral implants are better documented than bicep ones, mostly in reconstructive settings. In looksmaxxing it sits under hardmaxxing as a surgical alternative to training. Independent studies of cosmetic use in healthy men were not found, and much public description comes from surgeon practice material.
quick.how: A surgeon places the implant under anaesthesia through an incision, often in the armpit for the chest, and the added bulk shows once healed. It is usually chosen by people who want size beyond what training has given them.
quick.risks: Reported risks include bleeding, infection, hematoma or seroma, shifting, asymmetry, numbness and scarring. Silicone devices are regulated as medical devices.

angle.text: Solid silicone implants placed over the chest or arm muscle add bulk and definition, visible after healing. Pectoral implants are better documented, mostly in reconstruction; independent evidence on cosmetic use in healthy men was not found.

skin-bleaching-injections-glutathione-iv.summary: IV glutathione drips sold to lighten skin and even out undertones; a 2016 review found no evidence proving it works for this, and a regulator has warned about it.

quick.overview:
Glutathione is an antioxidant the body makes. Some clinics sell it as intravenous whitening drips, promoted to lighten skin and clear undertones, and Wikipedia describes it as the most common agent taken by mouth to whiten skin. The payoff people want is a lighter, more even skin tone.

It is said to inhibit tyrosinase and shift melanin production toward lighter pigment. A 2016 review in the Indian Journal of Dermatology, Venereology and Leprology concluded that no evidence proves IV glutathione works for skin lightening, and Wikipedia says it is unclear whether glutathione works. In looksmaxxing communities it is sometimes discussed as a way to lighten skin tone or undertones.
quick.how: It is offered in clinics and spas as a series of IV sessions, alongside oral and topical glutathione products. Any change in tone is described as gradual, with repeat sessions marketed to keep it.
quick.risks: The Philippine drug regulator issued a warning against IV use after adverse effects, and the Philippine government advises against it. The 2016 review found evidence for safety and efficacy limited. People with pigment concerns can ask a dermatologist about options.

angle.text: IV glutathione is sold as a whitening drip, promoted to reduce melanin and give a lighter, more even skin tone. A 2016 review found no evidence proving it lightens skin, and a regulator has warned against IV use.

eye-color-change-surgery-keratopigmentat.summary: Surgery that changes apparent eye colour with an implant in front of the iris or pigment in the cornea; reports mainly document complications.

quick.overview:
Two kinds of procedure aim to change the apparent colour of healthy eyes: cosmetic iris implants, such as NewColorIris and BrightOcular, which are silicone discs placed in front of the natural iris, and keratopigmentation, which tints the cornea. The payoff people want is a different eye colour, visible as soon as the procedure is done.

Implants cover the natural iris with a coloured disc, while keratopigmentation deposits pigment in corneal layers, with femtosecond lasers used in newer versions. Published literature on cosmetic iris implants is largely case reports and case series. A 2023 review states that iris implants were designed for conditions such as aniridia and are not approved by regulators anywhere for cosmetic use in healthy eyes.
quick.how: Both are eye surgeries done by ophthalmic surgeons, often abroad, with the colour change visible once the eye heals. Some people consider coloured contact lenses as a non-surgical alternative.
quick.risks: Reported problems include corneal decompensation or damage, raised eye pressure and glaucoma, inflammation and vision loss. Cosmetic iris implants are not approved by regulators anywhere, and vision-threatening complications are the main finding in the literature.

angle.text: An implant or corneal pigment changes the apparent colour of the iris, so the colour shift is visible once the procedure is done. Published reports mainly document complications, and cosmetic iris implants are not approved by regulators.

penis-enlargement-surgery.summary: Surgical or filler procedures for added penile length or girth; urology bodies say safety and efficacy are unproven and complications are documented.

quick.overview:
Penis enlargement surgery covers suspensory ligament release, fat injection or grafting, dermal fillers and silicone or PMMA injection, aiming for added length or girth and the body confidence that goes with it. Wikipedia states it is not medically indicated except for micropenis.

Procedures either release ligament attachments to expose more length, or add volume with fat, filler or grafts. The American Urological Association says fat injection for girth and ligament division for length have not been shown safe or efficacious, and the Sexual Medicine Society of North America issued a 2024 position statement advising against permanent fillers. A 2024 systematic review examined outcomes, complications and quality of life after penile augmentation. In looksmaxxing culture the topic is grouped under hardmaxxing.
quick.how: These are performed by surgeons or clinics, with recovery over weeks and sometimes post-operative stretching routines. Urology societies describe the evidence as limited and low quality.
quick.risks: Reported harms include scarring, shortening, deformity, infection, necrosis and erectile dysfunction. Fillers are not FDA-approved for this use, and professional bodies advise caution.

angle.text: Surgery or filler adds penile length or girth, which men link to greater body confidence. Urology bodies describe safety and efficacy as unproven, and complications are documented in the literature.

bonesmashing.summary: Striking your own facial bones in the hope of a sharper jaw and cheekbones; no study has tested it and surgeons warn of fractures and nerve damage.

quick.overview:
Bonesmashing means striking facial bones, often with a hammer, in the hope of remodeling them into a more defined, chiselled shape, with a sharper jaw and cheekbones as the payoff. It belongs to the bonehacks category of looksmaxxing, and Wikipedia describes it as rarely carried out and something of an inside joke.

Believers say repeated impact stimulates bone to remodel, a mechanism that has not been studied for facial aesthetics. No clinical study has tested whether it changes facial structure. Letters in oral and maxillofacial surgery journals in 2024 described it as a dangerous trend spread on TikTok, and a 2026 cross-sectional study of social-media discourse recorded thousands of mentions of the term.
quick.how: People describe striking the jaw or cheekbones with a hammer or similar object over time. Visible changes that users report are often attributed to other factors such as puberty.
quick.risks: Surgeons cite fractures, misalignment, neurovascular injury, deformity and vision changes as possible outcomes, and Wikipedia cites sources classing it as misinformation.

angle.text: Bonesmashing is a bonehacks practice in which people strike their own facial bones, believing impact remodels them into a more defined jaw and cheekbones. No study has tested this, and visible changes are often attributed to other factors such as puberty.

jawline-hammer-tools.summary: Hammers and similar tools for striking the face in the hope of a more defined jawline; untested in studies, with surgeons warning of fractures and nerve injury.

quick.overview:
Jawline hammer tools, also called face hammers, are hammers or similar implements marketed or discussed for striking the face and jaw, with the aim of a more defined jawline and cheekbones. They are associated with bonesmashing, the idea that hitting facial bones can remodel them.

Proponents say repeated impact stimulates bone to remodel. No published study has tested these tools, and the sources available describe the practice mainly through media coverage and surgeon commentary. Surgeons writing in journals describe the trend as dangerous.
quick.how: People describe using the tool to strike the jaw or cheekbones repeatedly over time, as part of the wider bonehacks category of looksmaxxing.
quick.risks: Facial surgeons cite fractures, misalignment, neurovascular injury, deformity and vision changes as possible outcomes.

angle.text: Face hammers are discussed as tools for bonesmashing, with users hoping that striking the jaw and cheekbones remodels bone into a more defined jawline. No study has tested this, and surgeons have warned about fractures and nerve injury.
